clue.text: Chuck down at least sixteen feet of water?

definitions.text: Chuck down at least sixteen feet of water?

parts.words: Chuck down at least sixteen feet of water?
parts.note: a downpour so heavy it seems to throw down two four-legged pets, so at least sixteen feet in all

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurl a huge quantity of water downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck down' is the plain sense, to pour with rain; the 'sixteen feet' is the joke: a cat and a dog have four feet each, and the plural idiom implies at least two of each.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes extremely heavy rainfall, water being chucked down from the sky.

clue.text: A flyer sending out a left-wing message?

definitions.text: A flyer sending out a left-wing message?

parts.words: A flyer sending out a left-wing message?
parts.note: a flyer is read as a bird or aircraft, but it is a banner that flies, and the colour of socialism signals a left-wing message

explanation.surface: A pilot or a leaflet broadcasting socialist propaganda.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner of the colour long linked to socialism and revolution flies as a left-wing emblem; it is also a warning signal.

clue.text: Teacher training trendy group of pupils?

parts.note: trendy means in, fashionable
a set is a group of pupils taught together by ability

explanation.surface: Teachers are trained to handle a fashionable class.
explanation.walkthrough: INSET is British shorthand for in-service education and training, the staff training days in UK schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names in-service training days for British schoolteachers, held while pupils stay home.

clue.text: Little son came last unfortunately, one of the others being in form

definitions.text: one of the others being in form

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters of son, came and last are jumbled

parts.note: little indicates the abbreviation S for son

explanation.surface: A small boy finished bottom, sadly, while a fellow pupil was on top form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges S plus CAMELAST. 'form' is the British word for a school class, not a state of fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow pupil in the same school class or form is another member of it alongside you.

clue.text: Trick gets mug

definitions.meaning: a trick or ruse set to catch someone out
mug is slang for the face or mouth, and so is this slang word for the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: One word means a snare or trick and is also slang for the mouth, as mug is slang for the face.

clue.text: Hatred? State that's evil, without love

parts.note: to state is to aver, declare

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the evil word goes round love

parts.note: evil means sin, wrongdoing
love is O, zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Is hatred a condition that is wicked and loveless?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, putting O inside SIN to make SION.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong dislike or antipathy can be close to hatred, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Coast eroded finally and split

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word eroded

parts.note: a split is a rift, a break

explanation.surface: A shoreline worn away and cracked open in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coast' is a verb here, not a shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move along without effort, to float or be carried passively.

clue.text: Appropriate work opening pursued by a female at the Sorbonne

indicators.note: pursued by puts the French word after the earlier pieces

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a port is an opening, as in a porthole or gateway
une is French for a, feminine, as used at the Paris university

explanation.surface: A job vacancy is fitting, chased by a woman studying in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sorbonne is a Paris university, signalling French.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed or suitable, so appropriate for the occasion.

clue.text: Like a cricket bat in a match

definitions.meaning: a cricket bat has its cane handle joined into the willow blade by a splice
a match is a marriage, and slang for married is this word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means joined by a splice, as a bat handle is, and is informal slang for married.

clue.text: Different appointment — I quarrel coming in

indicators.note: coming in places I and the quarrel word inside the appointment

parts.note: an appointment is a date
to spar is to quarrel or argue

explanation.surface: Someone at a meeting arrives mid-argument and finds it unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate things are essentially different in kind, not alike.

clue.text: Force that is left to protect one in the Commons

indicators.note: to protect puts the outer letters around the politician as a guard

parts.note: that is gives i.e., id est
a member of the House of Commons is an MP

explanation.surface: A force is told to guard a politician in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in the Commons' is a member of the British House of Commons, not a commoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or force someone into action.

clue.text: The French exam coming after all the others

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A French exam is taken after everyone else's.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent item is the one arriving after all others, the newest.

clue.text: Drug being given to inebriate man? That's hard to understand

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
an inebriate is a drunkard, a sot
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: Giving drugs to a drunk man is baffling behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inebriate' is a noun here, a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a few initiates, so it is obscure.

clue.text: Blooming strange in school

indicators.note: in places the strange word inside the school word

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
strange means odd

explanation.surface: Something flowers oddly inside a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' is the mild British expletive, not flowering; 'school' means a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are intensifying curses, mild swearing used for emphasis.

clue.text: Girl needs to get calmer — a person of strong spirit

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
calmer means stiller

explanation.surface: A girl must quieten down; she is very spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strong spirit' means hard liquor, not character.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes whisky or other spirits by distillation; strong spirit means liquor.

clue.text: Good news after prison escape? It comes as surprise

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the jailbird is located again, welcome news for the authorities

explanation.surface: After a jailbreak, good news arrives unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into CON (a convict) and FOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound is to astonish or bewilder, much as a surprise does.

clue.text: Facts not in Genesis

indicators.note: not tells us the word in is missing from the facts word

parts.note: facts are information
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Bible's opening book is said to contain no facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genesis' looks like the Bible book but means origin or creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Formation is the act of coming into being, a genesis or origin.

clue.text: Day that conspirator perches on tree

indicators.note: in a down clue perches on puts the conspirator above the day

parts.note: Cinna is one of the conspirators against Caesar in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: A plotter sits in a tree on a certain day.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is a tropical tree whose bark gives the spice.

clue.text: Firm's very careful, not half improving only slightly?

parts.note: a firm is a company, CO, and the possessive adds S

indicators.note: not half drops the latter half of the careful word

parts.note: very careful means meticulous

explanation.surface: A company is very careful but only half-heartedly improves.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic change improves appearance only on the surface, not substantially.

clue.text: Snag at Cambridge? Backward student must try to do this

definitions.text: Backward student must try to do this

parts.note: a snag is a catch, a hidden drawback
being at university is being up, as at Cambridge

explanation.surface: A problem at Cambridge, where a slow student must try harder.
explanation.walkthrough: To be up is British usage for being in residence at a university such as Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who has fallen behind must work to reach the level of the others.

clue.text: Test gold before trading

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
trading is dealing, a deal

explanation.surface: Gold is assayed before it can be traded.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe trial or test of endurance.

clue.text: A rhetorical effect to add into stories

indicators.note: into puts the adding word inside the stories word

parts.note: stories are lies, fibs
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A storyteller adds a flourish of rhetoric to tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, a figure of speech.

clue.text: Time to have wonderful old-fashioned dancing

parts.note: ripping is dated British slang for wonderful

explanation.surface: A great time spent at an old-style dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripping means moving lightly and nimbly, as in tripping the light fantastic.

clue.text: Tar to lurch about in the waves?

definitions.meaning: tar is the black sticky substance from coal or wood

definitions.text: to lurch about in the waves?
definitions.meaning: a ship that plunges fore and aft in heavy seas is said to do this

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' suggests a sailor, matching the waves, but means the black substance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a black resin like tar and also the fore-and-aft rocking of a ship.

clue.text: The old woman attracted by Jock's charm

indicators.note: attracted by puts mother next to the Scotsman

parts.note: the old woman is mother, MA
Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A mother is drawn to a Scotsman's charisma.

clue.text: Hug not a plant!

indicators.note: not tells us the a is to be dropped

parts.note: a hug is a caress

explanation.surface: An instruction: do not embrace a plant!
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a small salad plant with peppery leaves.

clue.text: Rock event for students about to start

indicators.note: to start puts the about letter at the front

parts.note: C is circa, about
a rag is a British student charity event

explanation.surface: A rock gig for students is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG week is a British university fundraising tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crag is a steep rugged rock face.

clue.text: Composer producing tons after time off

indicators.note: after puts the tons letter behind the holiday word

parts.note: hols is British slang for holidays, time off

explanation.surface: A composer churns out masses of work after a break.

explanation.definitionFit: The English composer wrote The Planets suite.

clue.text: Blunder in play has National Theatre laughing maybe

indicators.note: in puts the blunder word inside the play word

parts.note: a mime is a play without words
to blunder is to err

clue.text: Eighteen parsons fussed about virgin birth

indicators.note: fussed about suggests bustling around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clergymen fret over the doctrine of a birth without a father.
